clauses.reason: The command is: "I hereby approve such seal as the official seal of the United States Court of Military Appeals." An approval is performed when it is given; the order has no delayed effective date, so it was performed on signing, September 28, 1951. The command was exhausted on that date and the lasting consequence is recorded in savings. State on 2026-10-14: terminated.

conflict_resolutions.NO_ORDER_IN_FORCE_ON_1989_01_20: The 1989 Codification reprints the order's text under a source line that gives its Federal Register and 3 CFR location; it shows the order was published and codified, not that an operative command remained. The order's only operative words are 'I hereby approve such seal as the official seal of the United States Court of Military Appeals', a one-time approval performed on signing, September 28, 1951. The Court's own 1953 rules repeat the seal description and cite this order, which shows the approved design in use as a consequence of the approval; that consequence is recorded in savings and is not treated as a command of this order that continued. The claim does not decide anything about the seal's status after 1953.

inventory_overrides.reason: The machine inventory treats the order as a single whole clause. The operative command is the sentence that begins 'NOW, THEREFORE' and ends 'Court of Military Appeals.': the President approves the described seal as the official seal of the United States Court of Military Appeals. The WHEREAS paragraph describes the seal and says its design accompanies and is made a part of the order.

research_rationale:
EO 10295 (16 FR 10011; signed September 28, 1951) approves a seal of office for the United States Court of Military Appeals: "I hereby approve such seal as the official seal of the United States Court of Military Appeals." The preceding recital describes the design and says the design "accompanies and is hereby made a part of this order". The command is a one-time approval that was complete when the President signed the order; the text has no delayed-effect wording. Under the 2026-10-28 evidence ruling the command is exhausted by performance on September 28, 1951, and the surviving consequence (that the approved design is the Court's official seal) is separated and recorded in savings rather than treated as a command of this order that continues. The dossier's machine own-term leads for this number come from the Court's later rules of practice, which are not this order's terms and are not used.
